cards.explanation: The answer is True. Ishmael and his ten men come to Gedaliah at Mizpah, and they eat a meal together there (Jeremiah 41:1). Ishmael was a member of the royal family and one of the king's chief officers. I think that meal had to be the quietest one ever served, friends.

The answer is Chaldean, friends. Ishmael killed "…the Chaldean soldiers who were there." along with the Jews who were with Gedaliah (Jeremiah 41:3). Gedaliah was the one whom the king of Babylon had appointed to govern the land (Jeremiah 41:2). That detail matters later in this story.

The answer is the house of the LORD, friends. The eighty men were carrying grain offerings and frankincense "…for the house of the LORD." (Jeremiah 41:5) They had shaved their beards, torn their clothes and cut themselves, and they still made the trip with offerings in their hands. I think that tells you how much it mattered to them.

The answer is weeping, friends. Ishmael "…went out from Mizpah to meet them, weeping as he went." (Jeremiah 41:6) The text tells us what he did, and it doesn't say why he did it. What he did to those men next is heavy.

The answer is "Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam," friends. That's what Ishmael said to the eighty men (Jeremiah 41:6). Gedaliah was already dead, and the men didn't know it, since the text says no one yet knew (Jeremiah 41:4). The invitation sounded friendly, and that's what makes it so chilling.

The answer is False, friends. The ten men said they had hidden treasure in the field, and the text says "So he refrained from killing them with the others." (Jeremiah 41:8) The ten were spared, while the others were slaughtered and thrown into a cistern (Jeremiah 41:7). This is a heavy part of the story.

The answer is across to the Ammonites, friends. Ishmael "…set off to cross over to the Ammonites." (Jeremiah 41:10) He took captive all the remnant of the people of Mizpah, including the daughters of the king. He was taking them away from Mizpah.

The answer is near the great pool in Gibeon, friends. Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies with him took all their men and went to fight Ishmael, and they "…found him near the great pool in Gibeon." (Jeremiah 41:12) Gibeon is where they caught up with him.

The answer is rejoice, friends. The text says, "When all the people with Ishmael saw Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the army with him, they rejoiced…" (Jeremiah 41:13) Then all the people Ishmael had taken captive at Mizpah turned and went over to Johanan (Jeremiah 41:14). I bet they were glad to see him.

The answer is False, friends, because the number is eight. "…Ishmael son of Nethaniah and eight of his men escaped from Johanan and went to the Ammonites." (Jeremiah 41:15) He came to Mizpah with ten men (Jeremiah 41:1), so ten isn't the number here. The captives had turned and gone over to Johanan (Jeremiah 41:14).

The answer is Egypt, friends. They stayed at Geruth Chimham, near Bethlehem, "…in order to proceed into Egypt" (Jeremiah 41:17) The text says they planned to go, and the next verse tells us why they wanted out. Remember this word, because it matters for what comes next.

The answer is that Ishmael killed the governor Babylon appointed, friends. The text says "…they were afraid of the Chaldeans because Ishmael son of Nethaniah had struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land." (Jeremiah 41:18) Ishmael did the killing, and the people were the ones who felt the fear. They wanted to escape the Chaldeans.
